about: Reviewed dispositions for survivors of scripts/assurance_mutation.py. Each entry names the module, the exact source text of the line, the family and the rewrite, so it survives renumbering. An entry that stops matching a survivor fails the campaign, so a killed or removed mutant cannot stay on this list.

dispositions.reason: The separator only has to keep one path from running into the next. Any separator that cannot complete a risk pattern across the join behaves the same, and the sentinel cannot; test_the_risk_signals_read_paths_case_insensitively_and_one_per_line pins that a signal never spans two paths.

The origin key is hashed into an opaque identifier. Changing its constant prefix changes every such identifier consistently and keeps them unique and deterministic, which is all identity requires; no caller reads the key.
As for the acceptance key: the human-acceptance and falsification rules hash their own key into an opaque identifier, and a different constant prefix still yields a unique, deterministic one.
The requirement identifier inside the key keeps each impact obligation unique whatever the constant prefix is.

The separator between task and origin only has to be a byte neither contains. Task identifiers are TASK- plus hex and origin keys are fixed words, so the sentinel separates them as well as the NUL does.

dispositions.source: return left if CRITICALITY.index(left) >= CRITICALITY.index(right) else right
dispositions.reason: The two comparisons differ only when both indexes are equal, and then left and right are the same criticality, so either return is the same value.

Raising the last level searched to 5 adds a search at a level no verifier can declare: descriptor_contract only accepts levels 0 to 4, and escalation stops at 4 on its own. The extra iteration finds nothing and returns the same unsatisfiable route.
Ranks are only compared with each other. Rewriting 0 to 1 or 1 to 2 in this tuple position keeps deterministic routes strictly ahead of the rest, so every sort gives the same order.
Rewriting 1 to 2 keeps falsifying capabilities strictly ahead of the rest in this tie-break, so the order is unchanged.
Searching one level further, to 5, reaches a level no verifier can declare; see DEEPEST.

dispositions.source: for entry in _supplying(specs, capability, level, minimum)[:1]
dispositions.reason: Taking the two best verifiers per capability instead of one only adds candidates ranked behind the best one, and the choice below takes the best-ranked candidate overall, which is the same.

normalized reads this key with a default of False. Renaming the key on an entry whose value is False leaves the default in its place, so the declared descriptor is identical; the entries declaring True are pinned by test_the_built_in_registry_is_exactly_what_it_declares and were killed.
current_for is only used as a filter condition, where None and False are both false. No caller compares its result to False by identity.

This break follows the check that nothing is outstanding. Continuing instead reaches escalation with that same empty list, which raises nothing, and the next statement breaks out of the loop; the result is the same.

dispositions.source: not artifact.parent.is_symlink(), "INVALID_PATH", "Evidence directory must not be a symlink"
dispositions.reason: Reaching this refusal needs a symlinked evidence directory, which this Windows campaign cannot create. test_a_human_verdict_refuses_a_symlinked_evidence_directory pins the code and message on POSIX, where CI runs it.
Directory modes are not enforced on Windows. test_a_human_verdict_artefact_is_private pins 0o700 on POSIX, where CI runs it.
File modes are not enforced on Windows. test_a_human_verdict_artefact_is_private pins 0o600 on POSIX, where CI runs it.
